newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee to spend $27 mln on safety concerns. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee to spend $27 mln on safety concerns. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]

text.p: The Maine Yankee nuclear plant will spend $27 million in 1997 to address safety concerns about the facility, plant officials said Tuesday.
Management of the 24-year-old, 910 megawatt facility in Wiscasset, Maine also vowed to change the perception that the plant had downplayed safety in an effort to keep operating costs low.

"We will be cost efficient in the application of our resources, but we are no longer willing to let cost be the driving influence in our priorities," Charles Frizzle, president of the utility owned plant told reporters.

The plan, which includes hiring 50 new workers, will hike operating costs 20 percent (Corrects from 27 percent) above original projections for 1997. The new employees will increase costs by 10 percent annually in later years.

Maine Yankee's electricity is expected to cost 4.7 cents per kw/h in 1997 compared to an average of 3.5 cents in 1996, but will begin dropping to "historic averages" beginning in 1998, officials said.
Maine Yankee released the plan in response to a special review of the plant's equipment and operating procedures by the the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and state officials.

Governor Angus King requested the review in response to questions about the licensing of the plant's emergency core cooling system in the 1980s. The licensing is also being reviewed by the Justice Department.
The plan does not require NRC approval. Maine Yankee's board is expected to give its approval Friday. The board has also requested an independent review of Maine Yankee's management personnel.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co. and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
